Subject: EU-West compatibility sweep + fallback plan — Apr 27–29 (notice)

Hi Tom and team,

Quick heads-up: we're planning a compatibility sweep in eu-west (primary region) the week of Apr 27–29 to validate a new kernel/driver matrix against our serving runtime for a subset of models. This is a controlled, rolling operation intended to reduce future emergency restarts; we do not expect broad customer-facing downtime, but a small fraction of requests may experience transient reconnects as nodes are drained and validated.

High-level details:
- Window: Apr 27 22:00 UTC — Apr 29 06:00 UTC (staggered per AZ, see runbook).
- Scope: kernel and NIC driver updates + model-serving compatibility tests for the 1.3x family and samplers we run in eu-west.
- Expected impact: brief 5–20s reconnects for a subset of multi-token streams. Estimated p95 latency spike to remain under 2x baseline; estimated <2% request error increase at peak.
- Mitigations: continuous-batching briefly disabled on drained hosts, automatic fallback routing to a compatible quantized model variant, KV-prefix preservation where possible, and retry guidelines applied at the edge.

Actions for EdgeWorks / customers:
- If you have dedicated pools pinned to specific kernel images, please reply and we will schedule a targeted coordination slot.
- If you rely on long-lived streaming sessions, consider enabling client-side retry/backoff during the window. We can provide sample retry logic.

Internal asks (cc’d):
- Grace: please validate the fallback routing thresholds and share the updated impact matrix.
- Vanessa: prepare CS outreach for customers with high sustained connections; include the billing credit policy if we observe errors exceeding SLOs.
- Jonas: ops runbook is attached — can you confirm the stagger plan for AZ drains?

Attachments: eu-west-compatibility-runbook.pdf (runbook), impact-matrix-eu-west.csv (expected per-model impact), fallback-routing-snippets.txt (edge snippets).

We’ll follow up with a short pre-window note 48 hours before and a post-window summary + RCA.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 07:12, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick heads-up: we're planning a compatibility sweep in eu-west ...

Hi Tom — short answers:
- Dedicated pools: we will not reassign or route customer-dedicated capacity to shared pools. If a customer is on a reserved/dedicated pool and has pinned kernel/driver constraints, we will schedule a maintenance slot and do a non-disruptive rolling validation inside that pool with explicit consent. The fallback routing mentioned is for hosted/shared capacity only.
- KV handling: default behavior is to snapshot and rehydrate where feasible; for very large KV states we will fall back to prefix-only preservation and document the warm-up guidance. We added a KV-preserve flag in the runbook that ops will respect for pinned customers.
- Credit policy: Vanessa is handling the billing policy, but the short version is automatic credits only when SLO breach > 1 hour cumulative for a customer in the window. Smaller transient spikes will be handled case-by-case via CS.

I'll attach a quick table of thresholds (included in impact-matrix-eu-west.csv). Grace

Grace O'Connor
Sr. Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
